title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from the notation and the 1976 divided-power de Rham context; the page does not define it):
- S_k is a graded one-variable algebra with basis T^{(j)}. The multiplication rule T^{(d)}T^{(j)} = c_{d,j} T^{(d+j)} strongly suggests the divided-power algebra Γ_k(T), with c_{d,j} the binomial coefficient C(d+j, d).
- M_{S_k} = M ⊗_k S_k is a graded module with M placed in degree 0.
- τ_α is the truncation 'part of degree ≥ α', an S-submodule.
- Hom^d means S-linear maps that are homogeneous of degree d.

The first boxed statement (a') is a stability lemma. One may compute degree-d Homs after truncating the source at N−d and the target at N, for N ≥ 0, when M* is in a class \mathcal{M}_{-d} (undefined here, probably modules generated in degree ≥ −d). Example: Hom^d(M⊗S, N⊗S) ≅ Hom^d(τ_{N−d}M_S, τ_N N_S) ≅ Hom_k(M,N) for d ≥ 0. Grothendieck then begins a systematic computation of Hom^d(τ_α M_S, τ_β N_S) for β ≥ α.

Case (a), d ≥ β−α:
- Any degree-d map sends τ_α into τ_{α+d} ⊂ τ_β, so Hom^d(τ_α M_S, τ_β N_S) = Hom^d(τ_α M_S, τ_{α+d} N_S).
- He claims this equals Hom^d(M_S, N_S) = Hom_k(M,N).
- Explicitly, u: M → N gives m T^{(j)} ↦ u(m) T^{(d)} T^{(j)} = c_{d,j} u(m) T^{(d+j)} for j ≥ α.

Case (b), 0 ≤ d < β−α (so β ≥ β−d > α): he starts comparing with Hom^d(τ_{β−d} M_S, τ_β N_S) ≅ Hom_k(M,N). This attempt is struck out and the case is left unfinished.

Purpose: bookkeeping lemmas on graded modules over a (divided-power) polynomial algebra and their truncations. These are presumably needed to compute Homs or Exts between filtered or truncated pieces of the divided-power de Rham complex, i.e. Hodge-type filtrations by degree.
errors: If S_k is really the divided-power algebra with c_{d,j} binomial, the identification Hom^d(τ_α M_S, τ_{α+d} N_S) ≅ Hom^d(M_S, N_S) fails in characteristic p. Over a field, τ_α Γ(T) is not generated by T^{(α)}, nor even finitely generated, so restriction is injective but not surjective. Example: p=2, α=1, d=0. A degree-0 endomorphism of τ_1 Γ(T) is T^{(j)} ↦ a_j T^{(j)}. S-linearity only imposes a_j = a_{i+j} when C(i+j, i) ≠ 0 mod 2, so a_1 and a_2 are independent and the Hom is bigger than k. The same objection applies to the boxed formula a' and its 'p. ex.' as stated. The statements are correct over a Q-algebra, or if S_k is the ordinary symmetric algebra, in which case c_{d,j} = 1 and the notation T^{(j)} would be odd.
Case (b) is struck out and unfinished; no result is stated for 0 ≤ d < β−α.
The class \mathcal{M}_{-d} in a' is not defined on this page.

ideas.what: Homogeneous Homs between truncations τ_α M⊗S, τ_β N⊗S of free graded modules over a graded (divided-power) polynomial algebra; stabilization under truncation
ideas.modern_name: graded module Hom computations / truncation of filtered (Hodge-type) graded modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard commutative algebra; in the crystalline setting, Berthelot, Illusie, Ogus

deep.surprise_reason: Routine scratch computation of graded Homs between truncated free modules, part of an unfinished case analysis. It is possibly flawed in characteristic p if S_k denotes divided powers. Nothing here appears new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: In case (a) the struck-out text is likely 'd ≤ 0' (or similar), replaced by the boxed hypothesis d ≥ β−α ('i.e. α+d ≥ β').
The final crossed-out display reads Hom^d(τ_α M_{S_k}, τ_β N_{S_k}) → Hom^d(τ_{β−d} M_{S_k}, τ_β N_{S_k}) ≅ Hom_k(M,N), marked 'rés.' (restriction) under the arrow.
In the 'p. ex.' line the lower Hom is Hom_k(M,N), with the subscript k replacing a crossed-out letter (not a degree d).
